items.stem: A call center stores recorded customer calls and wants to convert the audio into text transcripts. Which AWS service should the company use?

options.rationale: Amazon Polly converts text into speech, which is the opposite direction from this requirement.
Amazon Transcribe is the managed speech recognition service that converts audio into text.
Amazon Translate converts text from one language to another and does not process audio.
Amazon Comprehend analyzes text for sentiment and entities but cannot transcribe audio.

items.explanation: Speech recognition turns spoken audio into written text. Amazon Transcribe is the AWS managed service for this, and it needs no ML expertise because it is exposed as an API. The transcripts can then feed other services, such as Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis. Amazon Polly performs the reverse task, text to speech, while Amazon Translate changes the language of existing text.

items.stem: A company wants its mobile app to read written articles aloud to users in a natural-sounding voice. Which AWS service provides this capability?

options.rationale: Amazon Transcribe converts speech into text, so it would not read text aloud.
Amazon Lex builds conversational chatbots and is not the service for narrating articles.
Amazon Kendra provides intelligent search over documents and does not generate speech.
Amazon Polly turns text into lifelike speech, which fits reading articles aloud.

items.explanation: Text-to-speech is the capability of generating spoken audio from written text. Amazon Polly provides this as a managed service with many voices and languages, so developers can add narration to apps without training a model. The other services handle different tasks: Amazon Transcribe does speech to text, Amazon Lex handles conversations, and Amazon Kendra handles search.

items.stem: A retailer needs to convert product descriptions from English into several other languages for its international websites. Which AWS service is designed for this task?

options.rationale: Amazon Translate is the managed neural machine translation service for converting text between languages.
Amazon Polly generates spoken audio from text and does not translate between languages.
Amazon Comprehend extracts insights such as entities and sentiment but does not translate text.
Amazon Transcribe converts audio to text and is not used for translating written descriptions.

items.explanation: Machine translation is an NLP capability that converts text from a source language to a target language. Amazon Translate offers it as a managed service called through an API, which suits localizing content such as product descriptions at scale. Comprehend analyzes the meaning of text, Polly speaks it, and Transcribe converts audio into text; none of them translate.

items.stem: A company wants to train a model that labels each incoming email as either spam or not spam. Which ML technique does this describe?

options.rationale: Regression predicts a continuous numeric value, not a category such as spam or not spam.
Clustering groups unlabeled data, but this problem predicts predefined labels.
Classification assigns each input to one of a set of predefined categories, here spam or not spam.
Dimensionality reduction reduces the number of features and does not assign labels to emails.

items.explanation: Supervised learning problems split into two main types. Classification predicts a discrete category, such as spam or not spam, and regression predicts a continuous number, such as a price. Because the possible answers here are a fixed set of labels learned from labeled examples, this is classification. Clustering is unsupervised and finds groups when no labels exist.

items.stem: A real estate company wants to predict the selling price of a house from its size, location and age. Which ML technique fits this need?

options.rationale: Classification predicts categories, but a selling price is a continuous number.
Regression predicts a continuous numeric value, such as a selling price, from input features.
Clustering groups similar records without labels and does not predict a numeric target.
Anomaly detection finds unusual records and does not estimate a price for each house.

items.explanation: When the value to predict is a number on a continuous scale, such as a price, temperature or demand, the technique is regression. The model learns the relationship between input features and a known numeric target from historical data. Classification would be appropriate only if the goal were a category, for example whether a house sells above or below the asking price.

items.stem: A manufacturer wants to analyze photos from an assembly line to find damaged parts automatically. Which AI application area does this describe?

options.rationale: Speech recognition handles audio, but this scenario analyzes photos.
Natural language processing works with human language text, not images of parts.
Recommendation systems suggest items to users and do not inspect images for damage.
Computer vision enables systems to interpret images and video, such as detecting defects in photos.

items.explanation: Computer vision is the field of AI that extracts meaning from images and video. Typical uses include defect detection on production lines, object and face recognition, and content moderation. Speech recognition works on audio, NLP works on language, and recommendation systems predict user preferences, so none of them match the image inspection requirement.

items.stem: A marketing team has purchase data for thousands of customers but no predefined segment labels. The team wants to discover natural groups of similar customers. Which technique should it use?

options.rationale: Clustering is unsupervised and finds natural groupings in data that has no labels.
Classification requires labeled examples, and the team has no predefined segments.
Regression predicts a numeric value, but the goal here is to discover groups.
Image recognition is a supervised vision task and the data here is purchase records.

items.explanation: The absence of labels is the key signal. Unsupervised learning finds structure in unlabeled data, and clustering is the common technique for grouping similar items, such as customer segmentation. Classification and regression are supervised techniques that need a known target value in the training data. Once clusters are found, the business can name and act on each segment.

options.rationale: Amazon Lex builds conversational interfaces and does not analyze review text for sentiment.
Amazon Polly generates speech and does not extract sentiment or entities from text.
Amazon Comprehend detects sentiment and entities in text without requiring model training.
Amazon Transcribe handles audio input, whereas the reviews are already written text.

items.explanation: Amazon Comprehend is a managed NLP service that finds insights in text, including sentiment, entities, key phrases and the dominant language. It is called through an API, so the company does not need to build or train a model. Transcribe would only be needed first if the reviews were recorded audio, and Lex and Polly address conversation and speech output.

items.stem: A payroll system must compute income tax withholding using a formula defined exactly by law, and the result must be identical every time for the same inputs. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: Train a regression model on past payroll results
options.rationale: A model only estimates outcomes and could produce results that differ from the legal formula.

options.text: Implement the formula as deterministic code
options.rationale: A fixed legal formula needs an exact, repeatable result, which deterministic code provides.

options.text: Use a foundation model to generate each result
options.rationale: A foundation model is probabilistic and could return different answers for identical inputs.

options.text: Train a clustering model on employee records
options.rationale: Clustering groups similar records and cannot compute an exact legally defined amount.

items.explanation: AI/ML models learn patterns and output predictions, which carry some error. When a task requires a specific, exact outcome defined by explicit rules, such as a legally defined calculation, ordinary deterministic code is the correct and cheaper solution. ML is better when rules are too complex or unknown to write down but examples of the right answer exist.

items.stem: A small business manually reviews about ten supplier invoices per month. A consultant proposes building a custom ML model to automate this. Which factor most strongly argues against the proposal?

options.text: Invoices contain text that ML cannot process
options.rationale: ML and managed AI services can process text from documents, so this is not a valid objection.

options.text: ML can only be used with image data
options.rationale: ML works with many data types, so this statement is incorrect.
Automation does not always reduce accuracy, and accuracy is not the main issue in this scenario.

options.text: The cost of building and running the model outweighs the benefit
options.rationale: At ten invoices a month, the savings are tiny compared with the cost of data, development and operation.

items.explanation: A cost-benefit analysis should come before any AI project. Building, hosting and monitoring a model costs money and effort, so it pays off when it removes large manual workloads or enables something people cannot do at scale. For a very low-volume task the manual process is cheaper, so ML is not appropriate here even though it is technically feasible.

items.stem: A support team receives millions of tickets each month and wants to route each ticket to the correct department without hiring more staff. Which benefit of AI/ML does this scenario highlight?

options.text: Scalability and automation of a repetitive task
options.rationale: A model can classify very large ticket volumes automatically, which people could not handle at this scale.

options.text: Guaranteed identical output for every input
options.rationale: ML models make probabilistic predictions and do not guarantee identical, exact results.

options.text: Removal of the need for any training data
options.rationale: Supervised models rely on training data, so this benefit does not apply.
ML models still make some errors, so error-free predictions are not a benefit.

items.explanation: AI/ML adds value when it can apply learned judgment to very large volumes of work, automating repetitive tasks and scaling beyond what a team can do manually. Ticket routing is a classification problem, and the model can send low-confidence cases to humans. Models do not remove errors or the need for data, so the benefit is scale and automation, not perfection.

items.stem: A utility company wants to use several years of historical electricity usage data to estimate next month's demand. Which AI application does this describe?

options.rationale: Speech recognition converts audio to text, but this scenario uses numeric usage history.
Forecasting uses historical data to predict future values such as demand.
Object detection locates items in images, and no images are involved here.
Sentiment analysis classifies opinions in text and does not predict future numbers.

items.explanation: Forecasting is a common ML use case in which a model learns patterns, such as trends and seasonality, from historical data and predicts future values. Demand planning, inventory and capacity planning are typical examples. Predicting a numeric value over time is closely related to regression, which is why the technique is often described as a regression-style problem.

Amazon Transcribe is a prebuilt speech recognition service and not a general model-building platform.

items.explanation: AWS offers prebuilt AI services, which expose capabilities such as translation or speech recognition through APIs, and Amazon SageMaker AI, which gives data scientists and developers the tools to build, train and deploy their own models. Choose a prebuilt service when it satisfies the requirement, and choose SageMaker AI when you need a custom model trained on your own data.

items.stem: A bank must explain to regulators and applicants exactly which input factors led to each loan decision, using a structured table of applicant data. Which approach is most appropriate?

options.text: A large generative foundation model prompted with applicant data
options.rationale: A foundation model is harder to explain and is probabilistic, which conflicts with the strict explainability requirement.

options.text: A deep neural network trained on the applicant data
options.rationale: A deep neural network is difficult to interpret, so it does not meet the requirement to explain each factor.

options.text: An interpretable traditional ML model such as a decision tree or linear model
options.rationale: Interpretable models show how each feature contributes, and they fit structured tabular data well.
Clustering does not learn from labeled loan outcomes, so it cannot make explainable approval decisions.

items.explanation: The requirements decide between traditional ML and foundation models. Regulated decisions that need explainability, on structured data with labeled outcomes, favor simpler traditional models such as linear models or decision trees, because their feature contributions can be inspected. They are also usually cheaper and faster to run. Foundation models are better for open-ended generative tasks, but they are harder to explain.

items.stem: Which scenarios are good candidates for applying AI/ML?

options.text: Computing a fixed shipping fee from a published rate table
options.rationale: A published table gives an exact answer, so a lookup or rule is simpler and exact.

options.text: Printing a report of last month's totals from a database
options.rationale: This is a simple deterministic query that needs no model.

options.text: Flagging potentially fraudulent card transactions in real time at large volume
options.rationale: Fraud patterns are hard to write as rules, and a model can score huge transaction volumes quickly.

options.text: Checking that a password meets a stated length rule
options.rationale: A stated rule can be checked exactly with code and does not require learning.

options.text: Helping doctors by highlighting suspicious areas in medical scans for review
options.rationale: A vision model can assist human decision making by pointing out areas for an expert to check.

items.explanation: AI/ML is most valuable when patterns are complex, data is plentiful, and the task benefits from scale or from assisting human judgment. Fraud detection and medical image screening are classic cases, since the model supports people and handles volume. Exact calculations, lookups and fixed rule checks have a precisely defined correct answer, so deterministic code is more reliable and cheaper.

items.stem: A company is evaluating foundation models (FMs) instead of traditional ML models. For which requirements is an FM the more appropriate choice?

options.text: Generating draft marketing text and summarizing long documents with little task-specific training data
options.rationale: FMs are pre-trained on broad data, so they handle open-ended generation and summarization with few examples.

options.text: Producing a decision whose every contributing factor must be audited by a regulator
options.rationale: Strict explainability favors interpretable traditional models rather than large, opaque FMs.

options.text: Predicting a numeric value from a small, structured table at the lowest possible cost per prediction
options.rationale: A small traditional regression model is typically cheaper and faster for this narrow tabular task.

options.text: Supporting many different language tasks from one model without training a separate model for each
options.rationale: A single FM can be adapted to many tasks, such as Q&A, summarization and classification.

options.text: Running on a tiny device with no network connection and very limited memory
options.rationale: Large FMs need substantial compute, so a compact traditional model suits the constraint better.

items.explanation: Foundation models are large pre-trained models that can be adapted to many tasks, which makes them strong for generative and open-ended language work and for cases with little labeled data. Traditional ML models usually win when regulation demands explainability, when the task is narrow and tabular, or when operational limits such as cost, latency or hardware restrict model size.

items.stem: A company is reviewing proposed AI projects. For which proposals is deterministic code or the existing manual process preferable to an ML solution?

options.text: Detecting product defects in thousands of daily images from a production line
options.rationale: This is a high-volume pattern recognition task where a vision model adds clear value.

options.text: Calculating each customer's invoice total from fixed unit prices and quantities
options.rationale: The correct invoice total is exactly defined, so arithmetic code is better than a prediction.

options.text: Segmenting customers into groups based on browsing behavior
options.rationale: This is an unsupervised clustering problem, which is a good fit for ML.

options.text: Automating a task performed twice a year by one employee in under an hour
options.rationale: The effort and cost of building and maintaining a model far exceed the small benefit.

options.text: Converting thousands of recorded interviews into text transcripts
options.rationale: Speech recognition is a good AI use case and a managed service already provides it.

items.explanation: Good AI projects combine a pattern-based problem, enough data, and enough volume or value to justify the cost. Exact calculations should use deterministic code because a model only approximates. Very rare, small tasks fail the cost-benefit test, since development and operation costs would exceed the savings.

items.stem: Which examples are real-world applications of AI?

options.text: An AI agent that plans steps and calls tools to resolve a customer request
options.rationale: Agentic AI systems pursue a goal by planning actions and using tools, so this is an AI application.

options.text: A spreadsheet formula that adds a column of numbers
options.rationale: Summing numbers is a fixed arithmetic operation and involves no learning from data.

options.text: A knowledge base that lets staff ask questions answered from company documents
options.rationale: A knowledge base that answers questions from documents is a common AI application using language understanding.

options.text: A scheduled job that copies files to a backup bucket every night
options.rationale: Copying files on a schedule is automation without any AI capability.

options.text: A firewall rule that blocks a fixed list of IP addresses
options.rationale: A static block list applies a fixed rule and does not learn patterns from data.

options.text: A model that predicts next quarter's sales from historical figures
options.rationale: Forecasting learns trends from historical data to predict future values, a standard ML use.

items.explanation: Real-world AI applications include computer vision, NLP, speech recognition, recommendation systems, fraud detection, forecasting, knowledge bases and agentic AI. What they share is that a system learns from data or interprets language, images or goals rather than just following a fixed rule. Fixed arithmetic, scheduled copy jobs and static block lists are ordinary automation, not AI.
